children: Maintaining production in Italy is a challenge due to increasing costs and competition, the European head of carmaker Stellantis
said on Thursday, calling for greater cooperation between industry, government and local authorities.

Emanuele Cappellano said Stellantis was investing over €5 billion ($5.5 billion) in research and development in Italy over the next five years, with 14 models being produced and another nine to be added by 2030, while spending more than €7 billion annually in purchases from local suppliers.

He said such figures confirmed the group's commitment to the country, though it was being made "more and more complex" by a difficult and constantly evolving context. Fiat and Alfa Romeo are among the Stellantis brands.
Cappellano cited rising production costs linked to current global conflicts, an increasingly competitive market due to rising vehicle imports and the costs associated with the electric transition.
"Under these conditions, ensuring the continuity of production that Italy needs becomes a daily challenge," he was quoted as saying during a conference in Verona by a company spokesman.

Stellantis is Italy's sole major automaker and its production in the country remains well below historical levels despite a slight recovery this year from the sharp downturn of 2025, when output fell 20% to about 380,000 vehicles, its lowest level in decades and roughly half the volume produced in 2023.

To support local production, Cappellano urged Italy to focus on curbing energy costs and cutting red tape, while adding Stellantis was holding talks with the European Union authorities on "pragmatic solutions" that address both environmental and industrial goals.
He said discussions on European local-content requirements and CO2 rules had shown promising progress in recent weeks and could result in new regulations by next spring.
